title: Hosted API cost bands by model and latency slice
summary: Working workbook that slices hosted API unit economics into discrete cost bands defined by model family, sequence-length bucket, and observed latency slice (p95 latency bands by region). Purpose: expose non-linear COGS drivers that get masked by pure per-token averages and produce recommended routing/pricing levers for each band.
assumptions: 1) List prices in the sheet are illustrative SKU-level prices (list_price_per_1k) for generation requests; prompt and completion tokens are aggregated into 1k token units. 2) Marginal token COGS is measured as per-1k token runtime cost (power, GPU cycles, memory) observed on the serving fleet for that model/seqlen/region bucket over the last 90 days. 3) Amortized GPU USD per 1k captures fixed VM amortization, host licensing, and infra overhead allocated to each 1k-token slice using weighted request counts. 4) Latency slices are derived from p95 per-route traces during normal traffic; low= p95<200ms, med=200-500ms, high>500ms. 5) Fallbacks (smaller model variant) introduce an extra "quality penalty" cost in the recommendations section and are not reflected in the raw cost rows. 6) Currency = USD, exchange amortization applied for eu/ap rows using average FX in last 30 days.
recommendations:
- Banded routing: route requests in seqlen <256 and low-latency slices to higher-capacity model families if margin positive; mark med/high latency+long seqlen as candidates for caching or pre-emptive truncation.
- Price bands: introduce a mid-tier price (list) for long-sequence generation >1024 when using larger models or provide a discounted bundle if customers accept lower SLO (serve from cheaper region).
- Fallback policy: automated fallback to open-mistral-8b for rw-13b long-tail when margin negative, with A/B evals to monitor quality delta; add a "quality escrow" surcharge if customer requires strict quality.
- Capacity optimization: move a portion of long-seq (1025-4096) batchable workload to reserved dedicated pools with lower amortization to recover ~30-50% of the excess COGS in the rows labeled 'high'.
- Billing flags & analytics: instrument per-request tags for seqlen and routing decision; surface band-level PnL in Console to ops and account managers.
notes:
Open questions and next steps: 1) Validate marginal_token_cogs for rw-70b — current sampling has high variance (need longer low-traffic window). 2) Confirm list_price_per_1k for enterprise negotiated customers (discounts change margin math). 3) QA the latency-slice mapping on eu-central during the regional network maintenance window (observed p95 shifts). 4) Run 2-week canary of banded routing in us-west1 with 5% traffic.
Quick wins: add per-route seqlen histogram to Console, export 30-day granular p95 traces for rw-13b and rw-70b to refine amortization model.
conclusion: This banded COGS view exposes that average per-token metrics hide significant loss-making pockets when sequence length and latency interact with model size and regional amortization. Immediate operational levers (routing policies, fallback variants, and dedicated capacity for batchable long-seq workloads) can recover margins without large price increases. Next milestone: run canary + refine marginal cogs for top 3 negative bands by 2026-04-10.
